exercises.name: Heeling
exercises.finishedPicture: Happy floating gate with ears and tail up. Precision - looking at me but not wrapped head and body parallel. Dogs shoulder even with my left leg. Floating gate with no stiffness.
exercises.criteria:
Expressive behavior/self-confidence
Particular attention is to be paid to expressive behavior by the dog during the judging and by
awarding the respective score. The dogs must show that they want to do the required exercise for the handler and not show that they are being pressured to do it. Close observation of the entire dog
such as facial expression, ear and tail position, tense muscles, unnatural movement, excessive
breathing rate, excessive salivation, or hectic behavior, etc., contribute to the evaluation. Negative reactions after the delivery of verbal commands leads to deductions.
Free, happy, motivated work
The dog should show motivated work. A strong willingness to work and to show a performance / execution of the work is top priority.
Concentration/attention
The dog must be concentrated / attentive to the handler during the entire routine without showing an extremely abnormal body or head posture (unnatural or robotic movement).
Harmony of the team
The presentation should show strong harmony in its work between the dog and handler. The dog must be able to follow the handler in a normal manner.
Technical correctness/position
In addition to natural expressive behavior and a harmonious performance, attention must be paid to the technically correct execution of the exercise. The exercises should be performed clearly and
according to their description.
Acceptance of commands and execution of an exercise
The dog should always accept the commands immediately and perform the exercises without stress or
delay.
Evaluation criteria for Heeling:
Running forging ahead, lateral deviation not remaining parallel to the handler, staying / lagging behind, slow, or hesitant reaction, sitting, requiring additional handler help with verbal commands, body movements, faults in the start position, inattention, lack of enthusiasm/motivation as well as
stressed / depressed behavior and lack of confidence of the dog lead to a faulty evaluation.

components.name: Precision
components.finishedPicture:
Looking at me but not wrapped head and body parallel. Dogs shoulder even with my left leg. 📝 Prerequisite Notes — Existing Canemo Precision Skills

Do NOT reteach these inside the Finish progression. These skills already live in Java’s Heeling → Precision work. The Finish progression consumes them.

Tuck / Rear-End Control: Java can bring her rear inward toward Kerrie and manipulate her rear independently enough to create correct alignment. Canemo specifically uses the tuck/pivot work to develop the rear-end movement needed for tight turning mechanics.

Back: Java can back straight while maintaining or returning toward the desired relationship to Kerrie. Canemo specifically treats backing as part of the physical skill set needed for rear-end/turn mechanics.

Lateral / Parallel Movement: Java can move laterally with Kerrie while preserving the desired spatial relationship rather than simply following a lure. This is already included in Java’s Precision foundation. FIELDWORK-backup-2026-09-30 3.json

Heel Seeking / Position Finding: Java understands where heel/basic position is and can independently find or correct toward it from different locations and angles. Canemo specifically progresses toward the dog offering the correct heel position while the handler remains stationary.

Around-the-World / Varied Starting Angles: Use the existing Precision position-finding work to establish that Java can approach the heel relationship from different places rather than memorizing one entry path. This is already represented in your app as varying Java’s starting location and angle. FIELDWORK-backup-2026-09-30 3.json

Prerequisite for starting Finish: Java has enough rear-end control, backing ability and understanding of heel/basic position that she can solve increasingly difficult approaches to heel without Kerrie having to physically lure the entire movement.

steps.name: 1️⃣ STATIONARY POSITION & BODY CONTROL
steps.goal: Java understands the spatial relationship of heel and develops the body-control skills necessary to find, maintain, and adjust her position beside Kerrie.
steps.actions:
- stand at different angles. 
* Release Java.
* Call Java into heel and have her find the position.
* Mix sit and stand arrivals.
- reward with raw food. 
- go back and get a handful of food and throw a piece of bull jack while after you get the piece of food. 
- as Java is running to get the other piece of food, change your angle and then call her back to Foose. 
- reward with the raw food and repeat. 
- make sure you’re keeping everything upbeat and active and fun and energetic
* Tuck: Java brings her rear inward toward Kerrie.
* Back: Java backs while maintaining/returning to the desired relationship.
* Lateral/parallel: Kerrie moves right and Java moves with her while preserving the relationship.
* Vary Java’s starting location and angle.
* As the individual movements improve, use them to refine small stationary positional errors.
* Keep changing where Kerrie relocates so Java learns the relationship rather than memorizing one entry pattern.

🎁 Reinforcer

FOOD OR TOY.

With raw food, deliver it normally. No throwing food.
steps.description:
This is the Canemo stationary foundation.

Finding heel, tuck, backing, lateral/parallel movement, and small stationary positional adjustments all live together here. They are exercises within one rung, not separate progression levels.

The purpose is to give Java both:

1. A map of where heel is.
2. The physical vocabulary to manipulate her body within that map.

Kerrie can release Java, relocate herself, ask Java to wait, and then call her back into heel so Java has to find the position from different locations.

Mix sitting and standing. The criterion is the spatial relationship—not teaching Java that finding heel always means sitting.

Canemo’s position-repair material similarly starts by establishing the desired location and then changing the dog’s starting relationship so she has to move back toward the desired
steps.todayJob: Find heel, move within heel, and refine the stationary position.
steps.criterion:
✅ Success Criterion

Java can repeatedly find the heel area and perform the tuck, back, and lateral/parallel movements well enough that those exercises are useful tools for creating the desired stationary geometry.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java has enough understanding of the position and enough body control that the next meaningful question is whether she can preserve that relationship when Kerrie starts moving.

steps.name: 2️⃣ MOVE THE SPACE TOGETHER
steps.goal: Java maintains the spatial relationship learned in stationary work while Kerrie makes small, controlled movements.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Start from established heel position.

Make small individual movements such as:

* small forward movement,
* backward movement,
* lateral/right movement,
* small directional change.

Mix directions rather than always using the same sequence.

Use the body-control vocabulary Java already knows rather than introducing an entirely new positional system.

Don’t turn this into sustained forward heel yet.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY from this rung forward.
steps.description:
This is the bridge between stationary Canemo body control and actual heeling.

Do not immediately turn Step 1 into long forward heeling.

Instead, Kerrie changes her location in small amounts and Java learns to move her body with Kerrie’s while preserving the relationship she already knows.

The important change from Step 1 is simple:

Step 1: Java moves within a mostly stationary heel picture.
Step 2: Kerrie’s space begins moving, and Java must move with it.

Ivan’s material similarly introduces attention with movement, then position while moving, including sideways movement and controlled walking before asking for more sustained
steps.todayJob: Move your space in small directions. Java moves hers with you.
steps.criterion: Java can move with Kerrie in several directions while preserving approximately the same spatial relationship she understands in stationary work.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Small movements of Kerrie’s body no longer routinely destroy Java’s position and you’re ready to isolate the first actual forward heel step.

steps.name: 3️⃣ ONE FORWARD HEEL STEP
steps.goal: Java transfers her positional understanding into one actual normal forward heeling step.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

* Establish correct position.
* Kerrie assumes normal forward orientation.
* Take ONE forward heel step.
* Evaluate where Java lands.
* Release/reward with toy.
* Reset.
* Repeat from varied setups.

Look at:

* forward/back relationship,
* straightness,
* appropriate lateral space,
* rear alignment,
* crowding,
* forging,
* lagging.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY.
steps.description:
This is the first true forward-heeling precision exercise.

Establish the desired position.

Kerrie assumes her forward orientation and takes ONE normal step.

Java’s job is to move forward with Kerrie while preserving the relationship she had before movement began.

Then reward.

This deliberately prevents duration from hiding a positional problem.

Ivan explicitly recommends beginning with one step and increasing the number of steps rather than doing enough that the handler ends up repeatedly correcting broken heeling. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf
steps.todayJob: Correct position → ONE normal forward step → toy.
steps.criterion: Java’s position after the step essentially preserves the spatial relationship established before movement.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

One normal forward step is no longer a meaningful positional problem and does not require repeated handler intervention to preserve the picture.

steps.name: 4️⃣ VARIABLE MICRO-HEELING
steps.goal: Java maintains the established heel geometry through short, variable amounts of forward heeling.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Use FIELDWORK’s randomizer for approximately 2–8 steps initially.

For example:

3 → 7 → 4

Perform that approximate number of steps while watching the positional picture.

Evaluate:

* forward/back relationship,
* straightness,
* lateral space,
* crowding,
* forging,
* lagging,
* crabbing/rear displacement.

Reward with toy according to the training plan.

Don’t let counting make Kerrie robotic. The number creates variability; it isn’t the fucking point of the exercise.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY.
steps.description:
Now turn one step into several.

The important new question is short-duration continuity.

Do not automatically build a predictable staircase of 2 → 4 → 6 → 8.

Use variable short stretches so Java learns that the position itself is the constant—not a particular step count predicting the toy.

This is still precision development, not BH-duration training.
steps.todayJob: Random short heel stretches. Same positional standard every time.
steps.criterion: Java can carry approximately the same heel geometry through varied short stretches instead of losing position as soon as she takes multiple steps.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Short moving heel is established enough that you can deliberately work on the specific positional errors that emerge during movement.

steps.name: 5️⃣ TRAIN ONE MOVING POSITION PROBLEM
steps.goal: Improve one identified moving-position weakness at a time using the most appropriate exercise from the systems Kerrie uses.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Before training, fill in:

TODAY’S POSITION PROBLEM: __________

Choose ONE.

Examples:

Forging
Use the appropriate Canemo backing, speed, reward-location or position exercise.

Rear out / crabbing
Look at the entire geometry—including Java’s front/shoulder relationship—then select the appropriate body-control or moving-position exercise.

Crowding
Train the desired lateral relationship rather than merely pushing Java away every time she crowds.

Too far laterally
Use established lateral/parallel body-control mechanics to clarify the desired relationship.

Lagging
Use the appropriate forward-position/reward mechanics.

Wrapping / loss of parallel alignment
Select the body-control/movement exercise that directly changes that geometry.

Keep the heeling short enough that you’re actually training the selected problem rather than rehearsing it.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY.
steps.description:
This is where we stop pretending Canemo, Natalia and Ivan need to become one giant unified religion. 😂

They don’t.

They become a toolbox.

Before the session, identify the actual positional problem you want to train.

Then choose the mechanics that best address that problem.

Canemo specifically discusses separate strategies for forging, lagging, crooked position, pushing/crowding and other heeling problems, including reward-location changes, backing and opposite drills. Canemo - Trained To Trial.pdf Their Heel Like a Champ material also notes that apparent crabbing can sometimes be connected to forging, which is exactly why we shouldn’t automatically attack Java’s rear whenever the picture looks crooked. Canemo - Heel Like a Champ.pdf
steps.todayJob: Pick ONE moving-position problem and deliberately train that problem.
steps.criterion: The selected positional problem measurably improves during short moving work with decreasing handler intervention while Java’s emotional picture remains intact.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java’s major moving-position tendencies can be addressed through known exercises rather than Kerrie constantly improvising corrections while walking.

steps.name: 6️⃣ REMOVE ONE HANDLER HELP
steps.goal: Java maintains the established heel position while one specific training-only handler aid is systematically reduced or removed.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Before training, fill in:

HANDLER HELP BEING REMOVED TODAY: __________

Possible examples:

* looking directly at Java,
* rotated head,
* shoulder orientation,
* exaggerated left-side posture,
* hand position,
* continuous leash information,
* another training-specific physical aid.

Use familiar short heeling.

Reduce one selected aid.

Leave the rest of the picture relatively familiar so you know what caused the change.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY.
steps.description:
Now we’re changing Kerrie, not asking Java to learn another positional concept.

The heel Java produces may partly depend on training-specific things Kerrie is doing:

looking down, changing shoulder orientation, altering her left side, using hand position, leash information, or another physical aid.

Ivan’s material specifically progresses the handler toward looking forward and warns that shoulder position changes the dog’s position; his notes call for the handler’s left side to become straight/formal. 

Canemo likewise warns that turning the shoulders during reward can contribute to forging because the dog follows the handler picture. Canemo - Heel Like a Champ.pdf

Do not write “use less help.”

Name the exact help.
steps.todayJob: Remove ONE named handler help and keep the same position.
steps.criterion: The selected handler aid can be substantially reduced or removed without causing a systematic deterioration in Java’s heel geometry.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can maintain her established position while Kerrie’s body increasingly resembles the handler picture she intends to use in trial.

steps.name: 7️⃣ TECHNICAL MOVEMENT PRECISION
steps.goal: Java maintains established heel geometry through one specific technical movement variable at a time.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Before training, fill in:

TODAY’S TECHNICAL MOVEMENT: __________

Choose ONE, such as:

* slow pace,
* fast pace,
* normal → slow transition,
* normal → fast transition,
* left circle,
* right circle,
* left turn,
* right turn,
* about turn,
* another already-trained BH movement.

Use the appropriate Canemo/Natalia/TWC mechanics if that movement exposes a positional weakness.

Do not pile five technical variables into one precision session.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY.
steps.description:
Straight forward movement is no longer the only problem.

Now ask whether Java can preserve the relationship when Kerrie’s movement changes.

This is not where you teach every turn and pace from scratch.

If a technical behavior needs its own task analysis, teach it separately.

This rung asks:

Can an already-understood technical movement happen without destroying Precision?
steps.todayJob: Choose ONE technical movement. Keep the established heel position through it.
steps.criterion: Java adjusts her movement to Kerrie’s movement while maintaining the established forward/back, lateral and parallel relationship.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The relevant individual technical movements can occur without repeatedly destroying the established heel geometry.

steps.name: 8️⃣ ONE REAL BH HEELING SECTION
steps.goal: Java maintains established precision through one realistic section of BH heeling while Kerrie handles normally instead of micromanaging the position.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

* Select ONE BH heeling section.
* Use the appropriate setup from the separate Heeling → Emotion progression.
* Enter normal trial presentation.
* Perform the section.
* Reward afterward with toy.
* Record what positional element broke, if anything.
* Take that problem back to the appropriate earlier precision rung in a later detail session.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY in training.
steps.description:
Now shift from detail work to assembly work.

Choose one actual BH heeling section and perform it as a section.

Don’t stop every few steps to repair every tiny imperfection.

This rung asks:

Does the precision we’ve built survive when the exercise actually looks like the exercise?

If something breaks, that gives you your next detail-training target.

Do not turn the remainder of the section into twelve corrections because Java’s ass moved three inches.
steps.todayJob: Run ONE real BH section. Don’t micromanage it—find out whether the precision holds.
steps.criterion: Java’s established heel geometry survives a meaningful realistic section without continuous training-only positional assistance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Individual BH sections are sufficiently stable that the next meaningful problem is connecting them without resetting Java between each piece.

steps.name: 9️⃣ CONNECT BH SECTIONS
steps.goal: Java maintains precise heel position when multiple BH sections are connected without a precision reset between them.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

* Select two established BH sections.
* Perform Section A.
* Continue directly into Section B.
* Reward after the planned connected work.
* Gradually connect additional sections.
* Track where positional deterioration begins.
* Pull specific failures back into detail work rather than endlessly rerunning the connected sequence.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY ONLY in training.
steps.description:
📝 Description

The new criterion is continuity.

Step 8 asks whether Java can perform one real section.

Step 9 asks whether she can finish that section and continue working.

Start by connecting two established sections.

Then gradually connect more.

You’re no longer rebuilding the entire precision picture after every successful piece.
steps.todayJob: Connect BH sections without stopping to rebuild Java between them.
steps.criterion: Java maintains the established spatial relationship across connected sections without consistent accumulation of forging, lagging, crabbing, crowding or other positional deterioration.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Connected BH work is stable enough that performing the complete heeling picture represents the next reasonable increase.

steps.name: 🔟 FULL BH — INDEPENDENT PRECISION
steps.goal: Java independently maintains the desired heel position through the complete BH heeling picture with Kerrie using normal trial posture, movement and cues.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

* Perform the complete BH heeling picture.
* Kerrie uses normal intended trial presentation.
* No training-only positional micromanagement.
* Record specific positional weaknesses.
* Repair those weaknesses in separate detail sessions.
* Return to full-picture work to verify transfer.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY in training.
steps.description:
This is the terminal behavior for Heeling → Precision.

The earlier exercises should now be largely invisible inside the finished behavior.

Java knows where heel is.

She has the body control to manipulate herself within that relationship.

She can move the relationship with Kerrie.

She can carry it through forward heeling.

She can maintain it through technical movement.

Kerrie no longer has to continuously manufacture Java’s position.

The early exercises do not disappear. They become your troubleshooting toolbox.

If full BH work exposes forging, don’t repeatedly run full BH heeling hoping forging disappears. Go back to the appropriate detail exercise, train the problem, and then return to assembly work to see whether the repair transferred.

And the separate Emotion progression remains active throughout this process.

A geometrically prettier Java who has become emotionally compressed is not the finished behavior.
steps.todayJob: Normal trial Kerrie. Full BH heel. Java owns the position.
steps.criterion: Java independently maintains stable heel geometry throughout the complete BH heeling picture without continuous leash, hand, body, visual or reward-position assistance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

There is no further Precision rung.

Move into maintenance, generalization, trial preparation and targeted troubleshooting while the other Heeling components continue developing.

steps.name: 1️⃣1️⃣ OFF-LEASH HEELING
steps.goal: Transfer Java’s established heeling picture from on leash to off leash without changing the behavior.
steps.actions:
Remove the leash and perform already-established heeling work.

Begin with familiar amounts of heeling and build toward the complete established picture as needed.

Use:

* straight heeling,
* normal pace,
* established pace changes,
* established turns,
* about turn,
* halts,
* established sections,
* eventually the complete established heeling picture.

Do not introduce a new technical heeling problem at the same time.

If something falls apart, identify whether the weakness is actually leash removal or whether an earlier Precision/Emotion skill needs repair.

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy.

Use the established Heeling Emotion/Precision reward strategy.
steps.description:
Java already understands heel position, body control, appropriate space, duration, pace changes, turns, connected sections, and the full established heeling picture.

Nothing new is being taught except:

The leash is gone.

Removing the leash should not change Java’s position, attention, emotional picture, or Kerrie’s handling.

This is the bridge that eventually allows the established heel to be used in later off-leash exercises. Those exercises are not part of this step.
steps.todayJob: Take the leash off. Nothing else about heel changes.
steps.criterion:
Off leash, Java maintains the same established:

* attention,
* straight and parallel position,
* appropriate space,
* consistent relationship to Kerrie,
* pace,
* responsiveness,
* and open, powerful emotional picture.

She does not begin forging, lagging, crowding, wrapping, crabbing, drifting, or losing attention specifically because the leash has been removed.

Kerrie maintains her normal trial presentation without using the leash as positional or attentional assistance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java’s off-leash heel is functionally the same quality as her established on-leash heel across the heeling work she already knows.

At that point, off-leash heel is established and can later be assembled with the motion exercises when you’re ready to build those separately.

components.name: Emotion
components.finishedPicture: Happy floating gate with ears and tail up. Floating gate with no stiffness.

steps.name: 1️⃣ WATCH — ATTENTION INSIDE THE GAME
steps.goal: Build true eye contact without changing the emotional game.
steps.actions:
Start from play.

Put the toy away.

Ask for Watch in an interesting way; Ivan allows sounds to help initially.

Look specifically for true eye contact.

The dog does not need to be beside the handler—the Watch behavior is isolated from position.

Keep the handler’s left side straight/formal and reward activity on the right side so reward mechanics don’t distort the future heeling picture.

When the dog gives the eye contact:

Release first → handler steps away → wait at least a moment → THEN produce the toy.

Do not simultaneously release and reach for the toy. Ivan specifically warns that overlapping these creates conflict and makes the dog concentrate on when the ball will appear rather than genuinely watching.

Play should be meaningful.

Ivan explicitly says don’t use a 1:1 ratio where one look gets one trivial ball event. One good look can produce an explosion of fun. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

For our DRE layer, look for:

👀 true eye contact + 🔥 active/animated/eager/expressive dog.

Do not reward eyes while ignoring an emotional collapse.

🎁 Reinforcer

Interactive tug/play.

Vary timing and magnitude enough that reinforcement isn’t mechanically predictable.

Sometimes leave the dog hungry for another round; sometimes give substantial play.

Do not become so stingy that the dog stops believing in the game.
steps.description:
Ivan isolates Watch from everything else.

The dog should understand Watch wherever the dog is, rather than believing attention only exists in heel position. Ivan specifically distinguishes true eye contact from a dog targeting the handler’s armpit or shoulder. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

For FIELDWORK, we’re also requiring DRE with the attention. A technically correct stare with a flat emotional picture isn’t our finished behavior.
steps.todayJob: True eyes. Real emotion. Then PARTY. 👀🔥
steps.criterion:
The dog understands Watch independently of position and offers true eye contact rather than targeting body/reward cues.

At the same time, the dog remains:

active
animated
eager
expressive
mobile
cognitively available

The attention should feel like part of the game—not the moment the dog switches into serious obedience mode.

The sog should not bark unless asked.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

True Watch is understood from different positions and can occur without meaningful loss of DRE.

steps.name: 2️⃣ SUSTAIN ATTENTION + DRE
steps.goal: Increase attention while preserving emotion, expectation and desire for the game.
steps.actions:
Begin with the established Watch.

Use stationary/basic attention where useful to develop sustained attention.

Keep the criterion high.

Increase duration carefully rather than mechanically adding more time every repetition.

Don’t always reward at the same point.

Mix:

quick success → play
slightly longer → play
short again → play
another duration → play

The goal is not to teach a countdown to reinforcement.

The dog should not know:

“After X seconds the ball happens.”

The handler is watching emotion at the same time as attention.

If the eyes remain correct but the dog becomes:

less animated
less mobile
less eager
more compressed
more mechanical

then duration has not actually improved.

Use meaningful play. Ivan specifically warns that if the dog doesn’t get enough play, the dog can lose trust and stop being excited. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf
🎁 Reinforcer

Interactive toy/play.

Variable timing and amount.

Frequently finish with the dog thinking MORE, while occasionally delivering the substantial “explosion of fun” that maintains belief in the game.
steps.description:
Ivan’s Stage 2/3 introduces sustained attention and uses basic position as an initial place to work because checking out is easier to expose while stationary.

Basic is a setup here—not an entire seated-obedience project.

Ivan then warns not to increase duration too quickly or teach the dog to walk while looking away.
steps.todayJob: Build duration of Attention + FIRE—not duration of staring. 🔥.
steps.criterion:
The dog sustains genuine attention while maintaining DRE:

🔥 active
🔥 animated
🔥 eager
🔥 expressive
🔥 physically ready/insistent
🧠 cognitively available
Quiet unless asked to bark 

Reward variability increases expectation and desire rather than producing frustration, distraction or emotional decline.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The dog can sustain Attention + DRE together without depending on one predictable reinforcement point.

steps.name: 3️⃣ ATTENTION + DRE ON FOUR FEET
steps.goal: Separate attention from sitting and establish Attention + DRE while standing and ready to move.
steps.actions:
Get attention without requiring Sit.

If the dog sits:

Do NOT correct the dog for sitting.

Ivan says the handler can lightly touch the dog to encourage the dog not to sit. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

Reward attention while the dog is on all four feet.

This matters because Ivan notes that when a dog has to rise from a Sit or Down, the dog may break eye contact during that transition. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

Also pay attention to handler proximity.

Ivan’s Stage 6 adds:

If the dog sits, don’t come too close.

Adjust the handler’s distance and continue rewarding:

Attention + Standing. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

Now layer our emotional criterion over that:

Don’t merely create a dog standing rigidly and staring.

Look for a dog whose body says:

“WHAT ARE WE DOING NEXT?”

Use play, movement and chase between opportunities so standing attention remains embedded in the larger game.

🎁 Reinforcer

Interactive toy/play, movement and chase.

Vary reinforcement timing and magnitude.

A brief reward can be useful when it makes the dog come back more animated and demanding another round.

If shorter/less satisfying rewards instead produce disengagement or environmental interest, give more—not less.
steps.description:
This combines Ivan’s Stage 4 and the relevant four-feet work from Stage 5.

Ivan explicitly warns against repeatedly doing:

Sit → Watch → Release

because the dog can learn that Watch belongs specifically to sitting and then struggle to maintain attention when movement begins. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf
steps.todayJob: Four feet + eyes + FIRE + ready to fucking move. 🔥
steps.criterion:
The dog can remain on all four feet with:

👀 true attention
🔥 animation
🔥 eagerness
🔥 expressive/mobile body
🔥 physical readiness
🧠 cognitive availability
Quiet unless asked to bark 

without repeatedly needing to sit to understand Watch.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Standing Attention + DRE are sufficiently fluent that movement can be introduced without movement being the first time the dog has attempted attention on four feet.

steps.name: 4️⃣ ATTENTION + DRE WITH MOVEMENT
steps.goal: Carry the established emotional/attentional picture into movement.
steps.actions:
Start moving.

Use different kinds of movement rather than immediately marching formal straight-line heel.

Move.

Change direction.

Accelerate.

Slow.

Run.

Chase.

Reconnect.

Move again.

Reward while the dog is on four feet.

The question is:

Can the emotional-attentional behavior MOVE?

Not yet:

Can the dog perform perfect formal heel for X paces?

Let the game flow:

attention → movement → chase → play → attention → movement

Vary reward timing.

Movement itself can sometimes function as part of the game/reinforcement.

Do not create:

3 steps → toy
3 steps → toy
3 steps → toy

And don’t make every repetition progressively harder.

🎁 Reinforcer

Interactive toy/play plus dynamic movement/chase.

Variable timing and magnitude.
steps.description:
Ivan’s Stage 5 asks for attention with any kind of movement and tells the handler not to be rigid.

The handler needs enough familiarity with the process to recognize/reward the dog even when the dog is ahead rather than requiring one predetermined picture before reinforcement. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf
steps.todayJob: Make the FIRE move. 🔥🏃
steps.criterion:
The dog maintains:

👀 genuine attention
🔥 active animation
🔥 eagerness
🔥 forward intent
🔥 expressive/mobile body
🧠 cognitive availability

while moving.

Changing pace/direction should keep or increase the game feeling rather than causing stalking, stiffness or mechanical following. No barking unless asked.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Attention + DRE reliably survive movement and the dog remains eager to continue playing the movement game. No barking unless asked.

steps.name: 5️⃣ MOVEMENT + POSITION / SPACE + DRE
steps.goal: Teach the actual handler-space/dog-space relationship while preserving Attention + DRE.
steps.actions:
Start with established Attention + DRE.

Go slowly enough that the dog can maintain attention.

Talk/make noises as Ivan describes if needed to maintain attention.

Go sideways to help create attention.

Then:

➡️ Gently step into the dog’s space.

Ivan specifically says to gently go into the dog’s space and encourage attention.

The dog will often shift in response.

Reward that shift + attention. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

This isn’t incidental. It is part of teaching the dog how the handler’s movement relates to the dog’s body.

Then establish the actual spatial concept.

Imagine:

HANDLER SPACE | DOG SPACE

The handler’s left hand can serve as the divider/reference.

Ivan initially describes opening the left palm next to the dog’s muzzle and keeping the hand relatively still in the middle for several steps.

The hand belongs between handler and dog—on the inside. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

If the dog comes into the handler’s space, Ivan describes using the handler’s left leg against the dog’s left leg to move the dog back toward the dog’s own space.

But it works both ways:

When the handler comes alongside the dog, the handler respects the dog’s space too. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

Use the leash to keep the dog in the desired area rather than repeatedly allowing the dog to get ahead and then correcting after the error.

Keep the leash/handler mechanics from destroying the trial body picture.

And throughout all of this:

DO NOT let spatial teaching turn the dog emotionally careful.

If the dog gets technically more correct but becomes stiff, stalky or emotionally compressed, the complete criterion isn’t being met.

Break back into movement/play/chase and re-enter the space game.

🎁 Reinforcer

Interactive toy/play, chase, acceleration and the continuation of the movement game.

Variable timing/magnitude.
steps.description:
Ivan does not simply expect the dog to magically find heel geography once movement starts.

His Stage 6 actively teaches the relationship using sideways movement, handler pressure into the dog’s space, leash management and deliberate spatial boundaries. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

And the sequence matters:

“You walk on position after eye contact. Not at the same time.” TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf
steps.todayJob: Teach the SPACE without killing the GAME. 📍🔥
steps.criterion:
The dog demonstrates:

👀 Attention: genuine eye contact/attention.

📍 Space: understands that handler and dog each have space and begins responding correctly to the handler moving into that spatial relationship.

🏃 Movement: can move within the developing geography.

🔥 DRE: remains active, animated, eager, expressive, physically involved and cognitively available.

The dog should not become careful and mechanical because position has entered the game. No barking unless asked.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The dog understands the developing spatial relationship—including responding appropriately when the handler moves into the dog’s space—while Attention + DRE survive.

steps.name: 6️⃣ MOTION — PLAY THE ACTUAL HEELING GAME
steps.goal: Combine Emotion + Attention + Position/Space + Movement into actual heeling that remains part of the game.
steps.actions:
Come alongside the dog.

Get into position.

Interact with the dog.

Wait for the emotional picture.

Look for:

active
animated
eager
expressive
forward
physically insistent
mobile/waggy
cognitively available

Then move.

Start with one step.

Reward.

Increase steps from there.

Ivan specifically says to be satisfied with small accomplishments rather than doing a pile of steps until the dog breaks and then needing repeated corrections. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

🏃 PLAY WITH THE MOVEMENT

Experiment with:

pace
speed
stride length

because Ivan explicitly notes that changing speed and step length changes how the dog moves beside the handler.

Find and reinforce the gait/pacing you actually want. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

And keep the larger heeling game dynamic:

heel → accelerate → run → chase → play

play → attention → position → heel

heel → pace change → explode out

run together → reconnect into heel → move → play

short heel → challenge → chase

The exact sequence should not become predictable.

The dog should experience actual heeling as part of the game, not as the boring thing endured to earn the game afterward.

📍 POSITION DURING MOTION

Use the leash to prevent forging.

Ivan’s notes specifically distinguish holding/preventing the dog from getting ahead from letting the dog forge and then jerking the leash afterward.

Keep the handler’s hand on the inside as appropriate to maintain the spatial picture.

Look for:

no leaning
true eye contact
desired pace. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

🎰 REINFORCEMENT

Don’t make the reward point predictable.

Sometimes:

one brilliant step → PARTY

Sometimes:

several steps → brief intense play → back into game

Sometimes:

pace change → beautiful emotional surge → reward

Sometimes the dog carries the picture farther.

Vary the amount of reinforcement too.

Some rewards deliberately leave:

“FUCK YES—AGAIN.”

Other times give the substantial payoff that keeps the dog’s belief in the game strong.

Ivan’s earlier attention notes are important here: inadequate play can make the dog lose trust and stop being excited. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

So “leave the dog wanting more” does not mean chronically underpay the dog.

The dog’s response tells the handler whether the balance is correct.

🔥 More animation, eagerness, physical insistence and desire to re-enter the game = good.

⚠️ Scanning, environmental distraction, emotional decline, mechanical work or giving up = handler stretched the reinforcement balance too far.

🎁 Reinforcer

The whole interactive game:

Toy/play.

Running.

Chase.

Acceleration.

Dynamic handler movement.

Another opportunity to play the heeling game.

Variable timing + variable magnitude.
steps.description:
This is where Ivan explicitly says:

Focus on the dog’s emotion.

He wants the dog excited and not stalking.

The handler comes beside the dog, gets into position, talks to the dog and waits until the dog looks like it is going to explode—including the happy/waggy picture—then rewards emotion + position. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

This is not:

play → stop having fun → formal heel → toy reward.

The play/emotion and heeling belong together.
steps.todayJob:
PLAY HEELING. 🔥

Not “heel nicely until the reward comes.”
steps.criterion:
The dog can move through the heeling game while simultaneously maintaining:

🔥 EMOTION / DRE
Active, animated, eager, forward, expressive, physically pushy/insistent, mobile/waggy and cognitively available. Excited rather than stalking. No barking. 

👀 ATTENTION
True eye contact/attention rather than reward/body targeting.

📍 POSITION / SPACE
Understands the dog’s space and handler’s space and responds appropriately to the handler’s movement.

🏃 MOVEMENT
Free, powerful, confident movement at the desired pace without leaning or mechanical stalking.

🎮 GAME
Entering heel does not predict the end of play. The dog can flow between heel, speed changes, running/chase, challenges and play without a major emotional category change.

🎰 REINFORCEMENT RESPONSE
Variable reward timing/magnitude makes the dog increasingly eager for another round rather than creating disengagement.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The dog understands Ivan’s core picture of attention + walking + handler/dog space + position, and can express it inside a dynamic heeling game without losing DRE when actual heeling appears. TWC 2 heeling - Ivan Balabanov.pdf

Global rule across all six steps: technical improvement purchased with emotional deterioration does not count as progress in this progression. The entire point is to develop the technical Ivan sequence while teaching the dog that the heeling itself is the fucking game.

components.name: Distractions
components.finishedPicture:
🏆 Finished Picture

Java can perform her established heel in a wide variety of environments while remaining engaged with Kerrie and functionally ignoring irrelevant environmental distractions.

She can notice the environment without abandoning the job.

Environmental difficulty is increased deliberately rather than randomly overwhelming her, and Kerrie can distinguish:

Java doesn’t understand the heel
from
Java understands it but this environment is currently too difficult.

The finished picture is a dog whose heeling is portable.

steps.name: 1️⃣ FAMILIAR HOME — NO PLANNED DISTRACTIONS
steps.goal: Establish a baseline showing that Java can access her current heel in a familiar, low-distraction home environment.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

* Use a familiar home training area.
* No deliberately placed distractions.
* Set Java up using her current Emotion work.
* Ask for heeling appropriate to her current Emotion/Precision level.
* Reward normally.
* Note environmental checking, loss of engagement, start difficulty, or recovery issues if they occur.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
This is the control condition.

Do not manufacture distractions yet.

Use a familiar training area at home and train the heel Java currently has.

This gives you something to compare against when distractions are added later.

The question is:

What does Java’s current heel look like when the environment isn’t meaningfully competing with Kerrie?
steps.todayJob: Heel at home with nothing deliberately competing for Java. Establish the baseline.
steps.criterion: Java can readily access her established heeling behavior in the familiar environment without the environment materially changing the picture.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Home without planned distractions is boring enough that adding one controlled distraction is the next meaningful question.

steps.name: 2️⃣ ONE PASSIVE HOME DISTRACTION
steps.goal: Java maintains her established heel around one visible but inactive distraction at home.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Before training, fill in:

TODAY’S DISTRACTION: __________

Place one passive distraction at a workable distance.

Heel:

* away from it,
* parallel to it,
* toward it,
* past it,

as appropriate.

Change distance before dramatically increasing distraction intensity.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
Now introduce exactly one environmental variable.

The distraction does nothing.

It simply exists.

This could be an object, equipment, food container, toy, unusual item, person sitting still, etc., depending on what you deliberately choose to train.

Do not start with Java’s hardest distraction.

We’re teaching:

“Things can exist in the environment and you can still work with me.”
steps.todayJob: Add ONE passive distraction. Heel around it without changing everything else.
steps.criterion: Java notices or registers the distraction but can perform her established heel without repeatedly abandoning Kerrie for it.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

One passive distraction at home can exist inside the training picture without becoming the entire fucking training picture.

steps.name: 3️⃣ ONE ACTIVE HOME DISTRACTION
steps.goal: Java maintains her established heel when one distraction moves, makes noise, or otherwise becomes active.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Fill in:

TODAY’S ACTIVE DISTRACTION: __________

Then control:

* distance,
* direction of movement,
* speed,
* duration of exposure.

Start easier.

Heel while the distraction is active.

If Java cannot function, change the setup rather than rehearsing twenty failures.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
The new variable is activity.

Step 2 = thing exists.
Step 3 = thing does something.

Keep everything else manageable.

Examples could include:

* a person walking,
* someone moving equipment,
* a rolling object,
* normal household/yard movement,
* another controlled activity appropriate to Java.

Start at enough distance that Java can actually solve the problem.
steps.todayJob: One thing moves. Java keeps working.
steps.criterion: Java can maintain/recover her established heel around one controlled active distraction without requiring constant interruption or management.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Movement/activity itself is no longer enough to routinely pull Java completely out of the work.

steps.name: 4️⃣ MULTIPLE HOME DISTRACTIONS
steps.goal: Java maintains her established heel when more than one familiar distraction is present at the same time.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Choose 2–3 previously successful distractions.

Arrange them so Java has enough room to work.

Heel through/around the environment.

Change your path so the distractions appear from different angles.

Reward normally.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
Until now you’ve isolated variables.

Now begin combining things Java already understands.

Do not introduce three brand-new hard distractions simultaneously.

This is combination work:

known distraction + known distraction.

For example:

person moving + equipment present.

Or:

toy visible + environmental movement.

The exact combination is yours.
steps.todayJob: Combine familiar distractions. Nothing individually needs to be brand new.
steps.criterion: Java can work while multiple known environmental variables coexist without needing each one individually managed by Kerrie.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The home training environment can become reasonably busy without Java’s established heel falling apart.

steps.name: 5️⃣ UNPREDICTABLE NORMAL HOME ACTIVITY
steps.goal: Java performs her established heel during normal, less-scripted home activity rather than only around staged training props.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Train during ordinary activity appropriate to the home environment.

Examples:

* people moving naturally,
* doors opening/closing,
* equipment being handled,
* vehicles/activity at a distance,
* normal environmental noises,
* combinations you didn’t deliberately choreograph.

Don’t manufacture chaos.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
Now stop controlling every environmental event.

You’re still at home, but the environment starts behaving more naturally.

The difference from Step 4:

Step 4 = Kerrie deliberately arranges several known distractions.

Step 5 = normal home life creates some of the distractions.

You are testing whether the learning survives when Kerrie doesn’t know exactly what will happen next.
steps.todayJob: Heel while home life happens around you. Stop scripting every distraction.
steps.criterion: Java can maintain/recover her established working state during normal home environmental changes without Kerrie needing to control every variable.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Home has stopped being a meaningful generalization challenge.

Now leave home.

steps.name: 6️⃣ QUIET COMMUNITY LOCATION
steps.goal: Java accesses her established heel in a new but low-intensity location away from home.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Choose a quiet community location with:

* lots of working space,
* low traffic,
* few people,
* few moving distractions.

Let Java orient appropriately.

Build your normal emotional setup.

Ask for short, successful pieces of her established heel.

Don’t use the first community session to prove she can do BH-length heeling at Lowe’s on Saturday afternoon. 😂

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
This is NOT “take Java somewhere busy.”

The new variable is simply:

Different place.

Novel smells, surfaces, visual picture, ambient sounds and context are already distractions.

Don’t add difficulty just because she looks good for thirty seconds.
steps.todayJob: New place. Easy environment. Find the same Java.
steps.criterion: Java can access recognizable established heeling in a quiet unfamiliar location without the novelty of the location dominating the session.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Changing locations itself no longer produces a major deterioration in Java’s ability to work.

steps.name: 7️⃣ COMMUNITY — ONE CONTROLLED DISTRACTION
steps.goal: Java maintains her established heel in a community location with one identified environmental distraction.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Before the session:

TODAY’S DISTRACTION: __________

STARTING DISTANCE: __________

Work at a distance where Java can access the heel.

Approach, retreat, pass or work parallel depending on the distraction.

Adjust distance before deciding the behavior has failed.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
Now isolate one community variable exactly like you did at home.

The difference is that Kerrie has less control over the overall environment, so choose the location and distance intelligently.

Possible categories:

* person,
* vehicle,
* cart,
* dog at sufficient distance,
* environmental noise,
* doorway/activity area,
* moving object,
* whatever is actually relevant.

Don’t write “work around distractions.”

Name the damn distraction.
steps.todayJob: One named community distraction. Find the distance where Java can still heel.
steps.criterion: Java can work around the selected distraction without repeated disengagement from the task.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Individual community distractions can be trained systematically rather than simply avoided or survived.

steps.name: 8️⃣ COMMUNITY — DECREASE DISTANCE
steps.goal: Java maintains the established heel closer to an already-understood distraction.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Choose a distraction Java has already successfully worked around.

Record:

DISTRACTION: __________

PREVIOUS SUCCESSFUL DISTANCE: __________

TODAY’S DISTANCE: __________

Decrease distance in sensible increments.

Heel:

* parallel,
* toward,
* away,
* past,

as appropriate.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
Do not introduce a harder distraction yet.

The new variable is specifically proximity.

Step 7 asks:

Can Java work with that thing present?

Step 8 asks:

Can Java work closer to it?

That is a clean progression variable.
steps.todayJob: Same distraction. Less distance. Don’t increase everything else.
steps.criterion: Java can maintain the established heel at progressively closer distances without a meaningful deterioration in her ability to work.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can work at realistic distances from common community distractions rather than requiring huge buffers around everything.

steps.name: 9️⃣ COMMUNITY — MULTIPLE DISTRACTIONS
steps.goal: Java maintains her established heel when multiple familiar community distractions coexist.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Choose a moderately active location.

Identify the primary expected distractions.

Perform short-to-moderate heeling pieces while several things happen around Java.

Vary paths and orientations.

Use distance strategically.

Don’t chase the hardest possible setup.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
Now combine environmental variables that have already been individually trained.

Examples:

people + carts.

vehicles + people.

dog at workable distance + pedestrian movement.

Novel location features + moving traffic.

The point is environmental complexity, not overwhelming Java.
steps.todayJob: Several familiar distractions at once. Same fucking heel.
steps.criterion: Java can maintain/recover her established heeling while several previously trained environmental variables coexist.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Moderately busy environments no longer require Kerrie to organize the entire session around avoiding distractions.

steps.name: 🔟 BUSY COMMUNITY — NORMAL LIFE
steps.goal: Java performs her established heel in naturally busy community environments where Kerrie does not control the distraction sequence.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Choose an appropriately busy community location.

Perform planned heeling pieces while normal activity occurs.

Kerrie does not attempt to control every environmental event.

Use good judgment about distance and setup.

If one specific distraction repeatedly causes failure, pull that category back into Steps 7–8 rather than repeatedly rehearsing failure in the busy environment.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
This is the community equivalent of normal home activity.

You are no longer arranging:

person appears → heel → reward → person disappears.

Real life happens.

People change direction.

Carts move.

Cars arrive.

Something makes noise.

Someone walks past.

The challenge is unpredictability plus multiple variables, not simply increasing raw intensity forever.
steps.todayJob: Let normal community life happen. Java stays in the job.
steps.criterion: Java can maintain or quickly recover her established heel through naturally changing community activity without requiring every distraction to be staged.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java’s heel is reliably portable through a broad range of normal community environments.

steps.name: 1️⃣1️⃣ NOVEL COMMUNITY — COLD START
steps.goal: Java can arrive at a new community location she has not trained in before and access her established heel without needing multiple acclimation sessions at that specific place.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

* Choose a genuinely unfamiliar but reasonable location.
* Allow appropriate orientation.
* Set Java up normally.
* Ask for her established heel.
* Do not spend half the session teaching heel again because the pavement changed.
* Repeat across different novel locations over time.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY.
steps.description:
This is where we test whether Java has learned:

“Heel works everywhere.”

rather than:

“Heel works at Home, Parking Lot A, Tractor Supply B, and Training Field C.”

The location itself should be novel.

You don’t need to make the location insanely difficult.

Novelty is the variable.
steps.todayJob: New place. First visit. Produce the same heel.
steps.criterion: Java can access recognizable established heeling on the first training visit to multiple unfamiliar environments.
steps.rule: The behavior is genuinely generalized rather than tied to a collection of practiced locations.

steps.name: 1️⃣2️⃣ GENERALIZED HEELING — ENVIRONMENT DOESN’T DEFINE THE BEHAVIOR
steps.goal: Java performs her established heel across varied environments and normal environmental distractions without requiring location-specific retraining.
steps.actions:
🏋️ Exercises / What You Do

Rotate locations and environmental pictures.

Include:

* familiar locations,
* unfamiliar locations,
* quiet environments,
* moderately busy environments,
* naturally changing environments,
* relevant distraction categories.

Don’t endlessly chase more extreme distraction levels just to prove something.

Maintain the behavior you actually need for sport.

🎁 Reinforcer

TOY in training.
steps.description:
This is the terminal behavior for Heeling → Distractions.

Java doesn’t need to pretend the world doesn’t exist.

She can notice things.

The finished behavior is:

The environment can change without changing what heel means.

Some environments or individual distractions may still require specific maintenance work. That does not mean the entire generalization progression has failed.
steps.todayJob: Change the environment. Keep the same heel.
steps.criterion: Java can perform recognizable established heeling across varied familiar and unfamiliar environments without requiring the behavior to be rebuilt at each location.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

There is no further Distractions rung.

Continue maintenance and specifically train any distraction category that exposes a weakness.

steps.name: Step 1
steps.goal: Java maintains the established heel position, attention, precision, and emotional picture without the leash, creating the starting heeling behavior needed before Sit in Motion and the later motion exercises.
steps.actions:
The judge gives the instruction for the start of an exercise. The handler removes the leash prior to starting the next exercise “Sit” (this may be done after leaving the group before obtaining the “basic” position or at the “basic” position).

Remove leash → normal setup → heel off leash.

Initially use familiar heeling sections and distances.

Include established elements as appropriate:

* normal pace,
* pace changes,
* turns,
* about turn,
* straight heeling,
* stops/halts.

Gradually move toward the amount and quality of off-leash heeling needed to enter the motion exercises.

Do not add Sit in Motion yet.

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy.

Use the existing Heeling Emotion/Precision reward strategy rather than creating a new reinforcement system just because the leash came off.
steps.description:
The leash comes off, but the heel does not change.

This step tests whether Java’s established heeling picture is actually independent of the leash and whether Kerrie’s handling changes when the leash disappears.

Do not use this step to rebuild heel from scratch. Position, attention, emotional state, pace, and handler mechanics should already have been developed in the Heeling components.

The new variable is simply:

Same heel → no leash.

This should be established before adding Sit in Motion, so the sit exercise is not simultaneously asking Java to learn the motion exercise and a new off-leash heeling context.
steps.todayJob: Take the leash off. Nothing else about heel changes.
steps.criterion:
Off leash, Java maintains:

* 👀 attention on Kerrie,
* 📐 straight, parallel, consistent heel position,
* 🐕 appropriate space without crowding, forging, lagging, wrapping, or crabbing,
* ⚡ the established open, powerful emotional heeling picture,
* 🚶 consistent position through established pace changes and turns,
* and 🎯 responsiveness to Kerrie’s normal trial presentation without leash assistance.

The removal of the leash does not meaningfully change either Java’s heeling or Kerrie’s handling.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can perform the established heeling picture off leash with the same quality she shows on leash.

Then proceed to:

➡️ SIT IN MOTION

components.name: 🐕 OFF-LEASH HEELING
components.finishedPicture:
On
instruction of the judge the handler / dog team return to the starting point and assume the basic
position. This is also the starting point for the next exercise. The handler removes the leash prior to
starting the next exercise “Sit” (this may be done after leaving the group before obtaining the
“basic” position or at the “basic” position).
Running forging ahead, lateral deviation not remaining parallel to the handler, staying / lagging
behind, slow, or hesitant reaction, sitting, requiring additional handler help with verbal commands,
body movements, faults in the start position, inattention, lack of enthusiasm/motivation as well as
stressed / depressed behavior and lack of confidence of the dog lead to a faulty evaluation.

exercises.notes:
BH - Heeling on Leash, 30 points
Execution of the exercise: On signal from the judge, the handler starts the exercise. Moving in a straight, calm, and attentive basic position, the dog follows the handler attentively, freely, openly,
straight / parallel to the handler, reacting quickly and attentively to the voice command for "Heel".
The shoulder blade of the dog must always remain in position in line with the handler’s knee / hip on the handler's left side and when the handler stops the dog must sit independently, quickly, and
straight without verbal command. At the beginning of the exercise the handler / dog team walks straight ahead with his dog for about 45 -50 paces without stopping. They execute a left about turn
and after another 10 to 15 normal steps the handler shows the running pace and the slow pace (both about 10 - 15 steps each) with the verbal command for "Heel". The transition from the running pace
to the slow pace and back to the normal pace must be carried out without intermediate steps and must be done with a verbal command for heeling for each speed change. After the last 10-15 normal
steps the team comes to a stop / halt. After a 3 second pause the handler / dog team go into a group of at least 4 moving people. In the group the handler and the dog must go around one person on the
left and one person on the right (in any order) and stop once in the group at or near a person. On instruction of the judge the handler / dog team return to the starting point and assume the basic
position. This is also the starting point for the next exercise. The handler removes the leash prior to starting the next exercise “Sit” (this may be done after leaving the group before obtaining the “basic” position or at the “basic” position).
troubleshoot: What if it was a toaster
What is not clear to the dog
Rhythm/ heart within the precision while you’re building
Technique/ then speed / heart within the technique- don’t move on or combine till you have both
Always chasing — go with the flow. It’s not about the recipe. Read the dog.
