steps.name: 1️⃣ BUILD THE FRONT POSITION — CORNER
steps.goal: Create a precise, deep, straight front position and build enormous value for being there.
steps.actions:
Exercises / What You Do

Use the corner setup from the Dave material.

Establish:

* straight front,
* deep position,
* centered head,
* head up,
* engagement.

Build a large reinforcement history for the exact position.

Alternate reward hands to prevent a directional bias.

No recall work yet.

No finish.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food, with high-value toy/release as appropriate.
steps.description:
This is position before movement.

Dave’s progression starts by using the environment to establish the picture. Java learns what Front physically means before we’re asking her to arrive there from distance.

The critical concept in your notes is:

Kerrie isn’t fixing Java’s front forever. Java is learning what correct feels like. Front - Dave Kroyer .
steps.todayJob: Build one fucking place: straight, deep, centered Front.
steps.criterion: Java comfortably assumes and maintains a deep, centered, straight front with engagement and correct head position.
steps.rule: Java clearly understands the physical front position, is comfortable in the corner with the spatial pressure and the next limitation is lure dependence rather than understanding where Front is.

steps.name: 2️⃣ FADE THE LURE
steps.goal: Java independently maintains Front without following Kerrie’s hand.
steps.actions:
Begin with the established position.

Reduce the lure quickly.

Hands become neutral.

Wait for Java to maintain the correct position independently.

Mark and reinforce the correct independent picture.

Continue alternating reward hands so reward delivery itself doesn’t bend the position.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food, with occasional toy/high-value release.
steps.description:
Your Dave notes are very explicit here:

lure → raise lure → remove lure → capture independent position.

The goal isn’t follow Kerrie’s hand into Front.

It’s find and hold Front without help. Front - Dave Kroyer .txt
steps.todayJob: Hands neutral. Java owns Front.
steps.criterion:
Java independently maintains:

* straight alignment,
* deep position,
* centered/up head position,
* engagement,

without needing the lure to hold the picture.
steps.rule: The lure is no longer necessary to maintain Front.

steps.name: 3️⃣ TAKE FRONT OUT OF CORNER
steps.goal: Transfer the established Front into open space without losing precision.
steps.actions:
Move into open space.

Use a mirror where useful rather than looking down and changing Kerrie’s posture.

Java finds Front.

Hands neutral.

Watch for and reinforce Java’s own micro-adjustments.

If the position falls apart, return to the environmental support rather than lowering the standard.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food, with toy release available.
steps.description:
Now remove the environmental assistance.

Your notes specifically say this is the same exercise in a harder environment. No recall yet. Java should maintain the same position without the corner/wall doing part of the work.
steps.todayJob: Same Front. No wall. Java finds the fucking position herself.
steps.criterion: Java maintains the established straight, deep, engaged Front in open space without environmental support or continuous handler assistance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Front is stable in open space and Java is beginning to make her own small positional corrections.

steps.name: 4️⃣ ACTIVE FRONT — PUSH INTO KERRIE
steps.goal: Make Front an active behavior, not passive parking.
steps.actions:
Begin from clean Front.

Invite a small active push into Kerrie.

Initially reinforce tiny correct increases in pressure/commitment.

Gradually require a brief hold rather than immediate touch-and-leave.

Keep straightness before adding pressure—don’t reinforce crooked pushing.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food, toy/play available to maintain intensity.
steps.description:
Dave adds active pressure into the handler.

Java should seek the position and maintain engagement rather than touching position briefly and mentally leaving.

Your notes specifically distinguish sustained active contact from “pecking”—touching in and immediately disengaging.
steps.todayJob: Java doesn’t just sit in Front. She fucking owns the space.
steps.criterion: Java remains straight and deep while actively seeking/holding the established front relationship rather than becoming passive or pecking.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Active Front is automatic enough that Kerrie can begin moving without Java abandoning the relationship.

steps.name: 5️⃣ BACKWARD MOVEMENT
steps.goal: Teach Java that Front is attached to Kerrie’s body, not a spot on the floor.
steps.actions:
Start in correct Front.

Kerrie takes one small backward step.

Java moves forward to restore Front.

Build gradually into several steps.

Don’t buy movement with crookedness.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food, with toy/play as appropriate.
steps.description:
Now Kerrie moves backward and Java maintains the established relationship.

Your notes progress from one step → 2–3 → eventually 5–10, while maintaining straightness, depth, and active pressure.
steps.todayJob: Kerrie moves backward. Java moves with her and keeps Front attached to Kerrie.
steps.criterion:
Java maintains:

* straight alignment,
* deep position,
* active engagement,
* centered head,
* and the front relationship

while Kerrie moves backward.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can comfortably maintain the relationship over several steps without drifting or losing activity.

steps.name: 6️⃣ FRONT FROM DOWN — SHORT APPROACH
steps.goal: Introduce coming into Front from a short distance without sacrificing the position already built.
steps.actions:
Java downs a short distance directly in front.

Call to Front.

Use a lure briefly only if needed to clarify the transition, then fade it quickly.

Mix:

* Down → reward,
* Down → Front → reward,
* reset,
* occasional play.

Don’t make every Down predict a recall.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy.
steps.description:
This is the first real approach work.

Dave starts extremely close—your notes say approximately 1–3 feet—and warns about anticipation.

Importantly, the notes say to balance reinforcement of the Down and Front, rather than hammering Java for wanting the newly exciting Front.
steps.todayJob: Short Down → Front. Come in fast and land in the position Java already knows.
steps.criterion: Java responds promptly and comes from the short down into a straight, deep, centered Front without creeping beforehand or requiring persistent lure help.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can approach Front from short distance without the approach degrading the established position.

steps.name: 7️⃣ LATERAL SELF-CORRECTION
steps.goal: Teach Java to move her rear end to preserve straight Front alignment.
steps.actions:
Start in clean Front.

Kerrie makes a tiny lateral movement.

Java adjusts her rear to restore square alignment.

Initially reward very small correct rear movement.

Train both directions.

Reduce handler support as understanding develops.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food.
steps.description:
This is where Front becomes self-correcting.

Dave’s concept is essentially a door hinge: front stays organized while the rear moves to restore alignment.

Without this, Java can know “Front” but still lack the physical answer when she lands slightly crooked.
steps.todayJob: Move Kerrie sideways. Java moves her ass and keeps herself square.
steps.criterion: Java independently makes controlled rear-end adjustments in both directions while keeping Front aligned to Kerrie’s body.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java understands lateral rear correction in both directions and doesn’t simply move the whole body forward/sideways.

steps.name: 8️⃣ PIVOT IN FRONT
steps.goal: Teach Java to maintain Front while Kerrie rotates.
steps.actions:
Start in clean Front.

Kerrie makes small controlled pivots.

Build:

* small rotation,
* quarter turn right,
* quarter turn left,
* increasing rotation,
* eventually larger pivots.

Java moves her rear to remain square to Kerrie.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food.
steps.description:
This extends the lateral mechanic into rotation.

Your notes explicitly call this the bridge between laterals and around-the-clock work and say not to move on until the pivot is clean.
steps.todayJob: Kerrie rotates. Java keeps Front pointed at Kerrie.
steps.criterion: Java remains straight and centered relative to Kerrie while Kerrie rotates in either direction, using her rear rather than drifting out of position.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can independently maintain Front through meaningful rotation in both directions.

steps.name: 9️⃣ AROUND THE CLOCK
steps.goal: Java finds a correct Front from multiple approach angles and fixes imperfect entries herself.
steps.actions:
Work around Kerrie’s clock position.

Start with easier angles.

Progress around both sides.

Let Java solve her alignment.

If she arrives slightly crooked, give her the opportunity to use the rear-end mechanics she already owns rather than immediately fixing her.

Keep distances relatively manageable because angle, not speed/distance, is today’s new question.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food, with toy reward available for intensity.
steps.description:
Now the previous body-control work gets used for its actual purpose.

Java no longer always approaches from twelve o’clock.

She learns:

Wherever I start, Front means the same fucking place.

Your Dave notes specifically say the dog should approach from multiple angles, land straight, and use the correction mechanics developed through lateral/pivot work. Front - Dave Kroyer .txt
steps.todayJob: Change the approach angle. Java still finds the same Front.
steps.criterion:
Java can approach from multiple positions around Kerrie and:

* find centered Front,
* maintain depth,
* remain engaged,
* and actively self-correct alignment.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can reliably solve Front from the full range of trained approach angles without heavy handler help.

steps.name: 🔟 DISTANCE + FULL RECALL TO FRONT
steps.goal: Add distance and speed without losing the precise, self-correcting Front.
steps.actions:
Start from a manageable recall distance.

Build distance progressively.

Mix:

* full recall → Front → reward,
* restrained recall → reward for speed,
* recall → Front → self-correction → reward,
* setup → Kerrie returns without calling,
* occasional release through Kerrie’s legs rather than Front.

That last variation preserves recall speed and prevents recall always means slam brakes into Front.

If Java begins anticipating, return to her instead of calling sometimes.

If speed starts destroying straightness, reduce the distance/drive question and restore Front rather than managing her into position.
🎁 Reinforcer

Toy for speed/intensity; food for precision.

That’s directly consistent with your Dave notes.
steps.description:
Only now do we put serious recall drive into the position.

Dave’s notes explicitly say:

Same rules apply → only distance + speed increase.

The dog must remain responsible for Front rather than Kerrie helping more because Java is coming faster.
steps.todayJob: Launch fast. Land straight. Java owns both. 🚀
steps.criterion:
From full trained recall distance Java:

* responds immediately,
* recalls fast and committed,
* approaches directly,
* enters deep, straight, centered Front,
* controls the arrival,
* and independently corrects minor alignment errors

without Kerrie leaning, staring, shifting, or otherwise parking her.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can reliably combine full recall speed + independent precision without one destroying the other.

At that point Fronts are established and move into maintenance/trial assembly.

steps.name: 1️⃣ HEEL SEEKING FROM INCREASINGLY FRONTAL ANGLES
steps.goal: Java uses her existing heel-seeking and body-control skills to independently find basic position from progressively more frontal starting angles.
steps.actions:
Place/start Java at an easy angle from which she can readily seek heel.

Ask for heel/basic position.

Gradually change the starting angle toward increasingly frontal positions.

Java can begin from a sit, stand or down—the developmental question is finding heel from the angle, not the starting posture.

Allow some early rear-end overcompensation rather than helping Java through an incomplete flip with Kerrie’s body.

If Java cannot solve an angle, make the angle easier rather than adding increasingly large handler gestures.
🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy.

Reward in correct basic position.
steps.description:
This is not teaching tuck, backing or heel position again.

Those skills already exist.

Now we’re applying them specifically to Dave’s flip-finish pathway: Java begins from different points around the front/left half-circle and figures out how to get herself completely into heel.

Kerrie’s body stays as neutral and stationary as possible so handler movement does not become part of the finish.
steps.todayJob: Change the starting angle. Java figures out how to get her ass into heel. Kerrie stays the fuck still.
steps.criterion: Java independently finds correct basic position from several starting angles around the front/left side without requiring Kerrie to rotate or lure her through the movement.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can solve increasingly frontal starting angles and the next meaningful question is whether she can solve the movement from true Front.

steps.name: 2️⃣ TRUE FRONT → FLIP FINISH
steps.goal: Java independently moves from correct Front into correct basic position.
steps.actions:
Place Java in established Front.

Keep Kerrie’s feet, shoulders and torso neutral.

Give the existing heel-seeking/basic-position cue being used during development.

Allow Java to solve the movement.

Reward complete arrival, not a half-finished flip that requires Kerrie to twist or gesture to get the rear the rest of the way around.

If Java repeatedly finishes halfway, return temporarily to an easier frontal angle from Step 1.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy.

Reward complete basic position.
steps.description:
Now the starting picture becomes the actual exercise picture.

Java already knows Front.

Java already knows where heel is.

Java already has the rear-end mechanics.

This step asks her to connect those known pieces:

Front → seek heel → completely organize into basic position.
steps.todayJob: Front → find heel. Java completes the flip; Kerrie doesn’t finish it for her.
steps.criterion: From true Front, Java independently flips completely into correct basic position while Kerrie remains essentially neutral.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Front → basic position is mechanically fluent enough that the movement can be placed cleanly under the Finish cue.

steps.name: 3️⃣ FINISH CUE → INDEPENDENT BASIC POSITION
steps.goal: The Finish cue independently produces the complete flip into basic position.
steps.actions:
Start in correct Front.

Give the Finish cue.

Remain neutral.

Java executes the complete flip and arrives in basic position.

Reduce any remaining accidental handler help.

If performance deteriorates when Kerrie becomes neutral, don’t start wiggling again. Return briefly to the previous grade and restore Java’s understanding.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy.
steps.description:
Now the movement becomes the formal Finish behavior.

The cue—not Kerrie’s shoulder movement, hand gesture, foot movement or lure—tells Java to leave Front and seek basic position.
steps.todayJob: Say Finish. Then shut the fuck up and let Java find basic position.
steps.criterion: The Finish cue alone reliably produces an independent, complete flip from Front into correct basic position without meaningful handler assistance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java understands the Finish cue independently and can execute the complete behavior from established Front.

steps.name: 4️⃣ FRONT → HOLD → FINISH
steps.goal: Put the established Finish into the actual recall exercise sequence.
steps.actions:
Finish now becomes the final piece of the already-trained recall chain.

Nothing new should be taught here.

Java already knows:
Recall. Front. Front hold. Finish. Basic position.

This grade simply asks whether those established pieces remain clean when connected.
steps.description:
Finish now becomes the final piece of the already-trained recall chain.

Nothing new should be taught here.

Java already knows:
Recall. Front. Front hold. Finish. Basic position.

This grade simply asks whether those established pieces remain clean when connected.
steps.todayJob: Connect Front and Finish without fucking up either one.
steps.criterion: Java recalls into established Front, maintains Front until cued, then independently performs the complete flip Finish into correct basic position.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The complete Recall → Front → Hold → Finish → Basic Position chain is reliable without anticipation or handler assistance.

Then Finish is built.

components.name: Finish
components.finishedPicture:
📝 Prerequisite Notes — Existing Canemo Precision Skills

Do NOT reteach these inside the Finish progression. These skills already live in Java’s Heeling → Precision work. The Finish progression consumes them.

Tuck / Rear-End Control: Java can bring her rear inward toward Kerrie and manipulate her rear independently enough to create correct alignment. Canemo specifically uses the tuck/pivot work to develop the rear-end movement needed for tight turning mechanics.

Back: Java can back straight while maintaining or returning toward the desired relationship to Kerrie. Canemo specifically treats backing as part of the physical skill set needed for rear-end/turn mechanics.

Lateral / Parallel Movement: Java can move laterally with Kerrie while preserving the desired spatial relationship rather than simply following a lure. This is already included in Java’s Precision foundation. FIELDWORK-backup-2026-09-30 3.json

Heel Seeking / Position Finding: Java understands where heel/basic position is and can independently find or correct toward it from different locations and angles. Canemo specifically progresses toward the dog offering the correct heel position while the handler remains stationary.

Around-the-World / Varied Starting Angles: Use the existing Precision position-finding work to establish that Java can approach the heel relationship from different places rather than memorizing one entry path. This is already represented in your app as varying Java’s starting location and angle. FIELDWORK-backup-2026-09-30 3.json

Prerequisite for starting Finish: Java has enough rear-end control, backing ability and understanding of heel/basic position that she can solve increasingly difficult approaches to heel without Kerrie having to physically lure the entire movement.
On the Finish cue, Java leaves a correct, stable Front and quickly and independently flips into correct basic/heel position, using her rear end to complete the turn and tuck fully into position. She finishes straight, close, and aligned, without stopping halfway or needing Kerrie to help her complete the movement.

Kerrie remains neutral and essentially motionless—no shoulder turn, stepping, hand signal, lure, or body language is required. Java understands that the cue means leave Front, seek heel, and fully organize herself into basic position.

The movement is fast, confident, and committed, and Java does not anticipate the Finish before being cued.

steps.name: 1️⃣ LEG\-OUT FRONTS — LEFT & RIGHT
steps.goal: Teach the dog to yield around the handler’s extended leg and finish in a completely straight, centered front.
steps.actions:
Left-side approach

1. Reset the dog to an area off to the handler’s left. Either:
  • Toss food to that area, or
  • Place the dog there in a Wait. No food or toy toss is necessary.
2. Set the handler’s stance with the left leg slightly forward/out and the right leg back. The feet are staggered, not together.
3. Call the dog into Front.
4. The dog approaches from the left, comes around the extended left leg, and moves its rear end into alignment directly in front of the handler.
5. Reward only when the dog finishes straight, close, and centered.

Right-side approach

1. Reset the dog off to the handler’s right using tossed food or a Wait.
2. Reverse the stance: right leg forward/out, left leg back.
3. Call Front.
4. The dog comes around the right leg and yields its rear end into a straight, centered front.
5. Mark and reward the correct finish.

If the rear end is crooked:

Use a small, controlled touch with the handler’s foot/leg against the dog’s rear area as a positioning aid to encourage the dog to shift and straighten. This is a gentle physical prompt, not a kick or correction.

Fade that help as the dog learns to move its rear end independently.

Work both directions. Do not allow the dog to become proficient on only one side.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy/play.

Tossed food can be used to reset the approach angle. Alternatively, use a Wait and reward only after the completed Front.
steps.description:
The handler deliberately staggers their feet to create a physical obstacle/reference.

The dog approaches from the side of the extended leg and must move around it to find the correct front position.

This develops rear-end awareness, body control, and independent alignment.
steps.todayJob: Around the leg → yield the rear end → straight front.
steps.criterion:
- Dog approaches around the extended left and right leg. 
- Independently adjusts its rear end. 
- Finishes straight, close, and centered. 
- Does not need repeated foot/leg assistance. 
- Remains confident and enthusiastic.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The dog understands how to navigate around either extended leg and independently straighten its rear end into front.

steps.name: 2️⃣ SERPENTINE / FIGURE-EIGHT FRONT PIVOTS
steps.goal: Develop continuous rear-end adjustment as the handler pivots around the left and right foot.
steps.actions:
**Left-foot pivot**

1. Begin with the dog understanding the left-leg approach from Step 1. 
2. Establish a correct Front. 
3. Pivot around the left foot, gradually changing the handler’s orientation. 
4. The dog follows the change by rotating its ass and yielding its rear end to remain centered. 
5. Initially use small pivots.
6. Reward correct adjustments.

**Right-foot pivot**

1. Repeat using the right foot as the pivot point.
2. The dog follows the handler’s rotation in the opposite direction.
3. Look for independent rear-end movement and straight front alignment.

**Build the serpentine**

1. Progress toward larger pivots around each foot.
2. Alternate left-foot and right-foot pivots.
3. Connect the rotations into a flowing figure-eight  serpentine pattern. 
4. The dog keeps adjusting to face the handler, rather than allowing its rear end to swing out of alignment.
5. Reward at variable points throughout the pattern.

**Handler assistance**

If the dog leaves its rear end behind, a gentle foot/leg touch can help indicate the needed adjustment.

Reduce that assistance as the dog understands the movement.

Don’t rush into a full figure-eight if the dog cannot maintain straightness through a small pivot.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy/play. 

Reward individual correct pivots initially, then vary reinforcement as the dog becomes fluent.
steps.description:
This is the extension of Step 1 and the actual **serpentine** portion Greg described\.

Rather than only calling the dog around a stationary extended leg, the handler now pivots around each foot, creating a flowing figure\-eight movement. 

The dog must continuously adjust its body and rear end to maintain the correct front relationship - a straight front.
steps.todayJob: Around the leg → yield the rear end → straight front.
steps.criterion:
- Dog approaches around the extended left and right leg. 
- Independently adjusts its rear end. 
- Finishes straight, close, and centered. 
- Does not need repeated foot/leg assistance. 
- Remains confident and enthusiastic.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The dog understands how to navigate around either extended leg and independently straighten its rear end into front.

steps.name: 3️⃣ LATERAL FRONTS — SIDEWAYS MOVEMENT
steps.goal: Teach the dog to maintain front position while the handler moves horizontally left and right.
steps.actions:
1. Begin with the dog in a correct, straight Front. 
2. Handler stands normally with both feet together. 
3. Take a small sideways step to the left\.
4. The dog moves horizontally to follow, adjusting its rear end and re-centering directly in front. 
5. Mark and reward the correct adjustment.
6. Reset in Front. 
7. Repeat to the right. 
8. Gradually connect multiple sideways steps in either direction. 

Important details

- The handler moves sideways rather than rotating around a foot. 
- The dog should move its whole body, not simply turn its head toward the handler. 
- Look for the quick rear\-end adjustment that brings the dog back into center. 
- Start with small lateral steps so the dog can solve the movement correctly. 
- Reward straightness and independent correction, not just following. 
 🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy/play, delivered to support a straight, centered front alternating hands.
steps.description:
Unlike the first two drills, the handler now has both feet together in a normal stance. 

The dog starts already in a correct Front. 

The handler moves sideways, and the dog must pop its body and rear end across to remain directly centered in front. 

This is lateral tracking of the handler, not circling around an extended leg.
steps.todayJob: Feet together → handler moves sideways → dog pops back into center.
steps.criterion:
- Dog begins in correct Front. 
- Handler moves left or right. 
- Dog independently moves horizontally to maintain front alignment. 
- Rear end follows rather than lagging behind. 
- Dog remains close, straight, eager, and confident.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The dog can maintain centered front through lateral movement in both directions without physical assistance.

components.name: Greg’s Serpentine Fronts
components.finishedPicture:
The dog independently finds and maintains a close, straight, centered front while approaching around either extended leg, following the handler’s figure-eight pivots, and adjusting horizontally as the handler moves sideways.

The dog uses rear end movement to maintain alignment instead of arriving crooked or leaving its rear end behind\.

exercises.name: Front and Finish
exercises.criteria:
On the recall cue, Java comes fast, freely, motivated, and directly to Kerrie and independently enters a deep, straight, centered front.

She understands front as a position relative to Kerrie’s body rather than a memorized approach path. If her approach is imperfect, she has enough body awareness to correct herself rather than relying on Kerrie to park her.

Kerrie remains neutral—no leaning, staring, shifting, hand targeting, or other pre-signals to manufacture straightness.

steps.name: 1️⃣ BUILD THE STOP RESPONSE
steps.goal: Java learns that Kerrie stopping predicts an immediate sit.
steps.actions:
Start together in basic position.

Take one step forward → stop.

At the stop:

* initially use the known Sit cue,
* light immediate leash pressure,
* lure/help as necessary,
* Java gets her butt completely onto the ground,
* immediately reinforce the completed sit.

Keep these as isolated stop repetitions rather than turning them into heeling sessions.

As Java starts anticipating the correct response to Kerrie’s stop, reduce the amount of help.

A spotter can be used if useful; Canemo specifically recommends one for this stage. Canemo - Heel Like a Champ.pdf

🎁 Reinforcer

Food.
steps.description:
This follows Canemo’s foundation directly: work the stop separately, taking one forward step at a time.

Initially combine Java’s known sit cue with light, immediate leash pressure and lure help as Kerrie stops. Canemo specifically uses the leash to create a sharper reaction to the stop and recommends moving the food away from the nose when asking for the sit so the dog can concentrate on sitting. Canemo - Heel Like a Champ.pdf
steps.todayJob: One step → Kerrie stops → Java’s ass hits the ground.
steps.criterion: Java is responding sharply to Kerrie’s stop and completing the sit rather than remaining standing, creeping forward, or needing significant help.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The stop itself is clearly beginning to trigger the sit and the next useful question is whether Java will perform it without the Sit cue/lure help.

steps.name: 2️⃣ MAKE THE HALT AUTOMATIC
steps.goal: Kerrie’s stop becomes the cue for Java’s sit.
steps.actions:
Continue primarily from very short movement.

Move → stop → Java sits.

Fade the verbal Sit cue.

Fade the lure.

Reduce leash assistance as Java demonstrates understanding.

Keep Kerrie’s stopping mechanics consistent enough that Java can learn the picture without Kerrie adding some giant fucking body cue that you’ll eventually have to remove.

Reward the fast, complete automatic sit.

If Java stops standing and waits for information, you’ve removed help faster than her understanding supports. Temporarily restore enough information to clarify the response, then fade again.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food.
steps.description:
Now remove the temporary teaching information.

We’re no longer asking:

Can Java sit when Kerrie tells her to sit?

We’re asking:

Does Java understand that Kerrie stopping means Java sits?
steps.todayJob: Kerrie stops. Java sits. No separate Sit command.
steps.criterion: Java automatically and promptly sits when Kerrie stops, without requiring the verbal Sit cue or lure.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The automatic response is established strongly enough that it can be tested out of actual short heeling rather than isolated one-step repetitions.

steps.name: 3️⃣ AUTOMATIC HALT OUT OF HEELING
steps.goal: Java performs the automatic halt while actually heeling.
steps.actions:
Begin with short, established heeling stretches.

Vary the number of steps before the halt so Java doesn’t learn:

three steps = sit.

For example:

short heel → halt
slightly longer heel → reward while moving
short heel → reward
different short heel → halt

Kerrie stops normally.

Java should independently sit.

Watch specifically for:

* extra forward steps,
* slow sit,
* partial/hovering sit,
* crooked sit,
* rear swinging away,
* anticipation of the halt.

If the automatic response disappears, return to Step 2 rather than repeatedly rehearsing shitty halts inside heeling.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or toy, appropriate to the heeling work surrounding it.
steps.description:
Now consume the established heeling behavior.

This is where Automatic Halt becomes part of Fuss rather than a separate little stop drill.

The new question is whether Java can transition cleanly from:

heel → Kerrie stops → immediate sit in basic position.
steps.todayJob: Heel normally. Stop unpredictably. Java owns the halt.
steps.criterion: Java transitions directly from established heeling into a fast automatic sit in correct basic position without a verbal Sit cue or meaningful handler assistance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The halt itself is reliable enough that the developmental question is no longer whether Java will sit, but whether the behavior survives variation in the heeling picture.

steps.name: 4️⃣ GENERALIZE THE AUTOMATIC HALT
steps.goal: Java’s automatic halt survives the different heeling pictures she’ll encounter in the BH.
steps.actions:
Put established halts after different amounts and types of already-trained heeling.

Include halts after:

* short normal heeling,
* longer normal heeling,
* technical heeling sections as those become established,
* and eventually the contexts where a halt actually appears in the BH picture.

Don’t drill every possible variation in one session.

Don’t turn this into a new heeling progression. You’re testing whether the established automatic response transfers.

Canemo later uses abrupt halts during faster heeling as a forging exercise, but that’s advanced troubleshooting/proofing, not the foundation of the automatic halt. Canemo - Heel Like a Champ.pdf

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy or food, depending on the surrounding work.
steps.description:
Now we stop treating the halt as something that only occurs after one familiar little stretch of normal heeling.

The rule stays identical:

Kerrie stops → Java sits immediately in basic position.

Only the preceding context changes.
steps.todayJob: Change what comes before the stop. Don’t change what the stop means.
steps.criterion: Across established heeling contexts, Kerrie’s halt reliably produces a prompt, complete, straight sit in basic position without an additional cue.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java’s automatic halt is stable enough that it can simply become one of the known behaviors consumed by BH clumping and trial preparation.

components.name: Automatic sit
components.finishedPicture:
While Java is heeling, Kerrie stops and Java immediately and independently sits in correct basic position without a verbal sit cue. The sit is fast, complete, straight, and aligned; Java does not take extra steps, forge forward, swing out, or require Kerrie to lure, leash, gesture, or otherwise help her into position.

This matches the BH requirement already in your FIELDWORK notes: when the handler stops, the dog sits independently, quickly, and straight without verbal command.

exercises.name: Automatic sit
exercises.criteria:
While Java is heeling, Kerrie stops and Java immediately and independently sits in correct basic position without a verbal sit cue. The sit is fast, complete, straight, and aligned; Java does not take extra steps, forge forward, swing out, or require Kerrie to lure, leash, gesture, or otherwise help her into position.

This matches the BH requirement already in your FIELDWORK notes: when the handler stops, the dog sits independently, quickly, and straight without verbal command.
exercises.notes:
Java already knows Sit and Basic Position. Do not reteach either inside this progression.

Her existing Precision work owns the geometry of basic position. This component teaches the new rule:

Kerrie stops → Java sits automatically.

steps.name: 1️⃣ BUILD THE GROUP ENTRY
steps.goal: Java enters the group expecting to remain engaged with Kerrie rather than becoming interested in the people.
steps.actions:
Set up the group initially with chairs or familiar neutral people.

Approach in established heel.

Heel toward group → enter → reinforce.

Then leave/reset.

At first, don’t automatically continue around everybody after entry.

Vary where reinforcement happens slightly so Java doesn’t create one exact geographic reward point.

With real people, reinforce before Java begins checking them out rather than waiting for attention to fail and then trying to recover it. Canemo explicitly emphasizes reinforcement while approaching and entering the group.

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy, consistent with the emotional heeling picture you’re building.
steps.description:
Don’t start by drilling the whole figure eight.

Canemo specifically recommends building reinforcement expectation on the approach and entry, initially heeling into the group, rewarding at the focal point, and repeating just that piece. If the dog is worried about or especially interested in people, they recommend doing more repetitions of the entry. Canemo - Trained To Trial.pdf
steps.todayJob: Entering the group makes heeling better, not flatter.
steps.criterion: Java approaches and enters the group while maintaining her established heeling engagement rather than orienting toward, avoiding, or becoming preoccupied with the people/objects.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Entry itself is boringly understood and the useful developmental question becomes whether Java can navigate around the group while preserving heel.

steps.name: 2️⃣ BUILD LEFT & RIGHT GROUP PATHS
steps.goal: Java maintains heel while navigating both directions around members of the group.
steps.actions:
Use the Canemo chair setup initially.

Work one direction at a time.

Do a partial path around one chair/person → reinforce during or immediately after good execution.

Then separately work the opposite direction.

For the tighter inside path, watch Java’s ability to bring the rear around rather than letting the ass drift outward.

For the wider/outside path, watch for:

* forging,
* acceleration,
* going wide,
* crabbing,
* attention leaving Kerrie.

Canemo specifically uses reinforcement during the turn, rather than waiting until after a shitty turn has already happened. Canemo - Trained To Trial.pdf

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy.
steps.description:
Canemo teaches the two sides separately because they create different mechanical problems.

On one path, dogs may accelerate, forge, crab, or swing wide. On the other, the dog needs the rear-end mechanics to tuck and follow the handler’s path closely.

The square/chair setup gives Java a clear physical reference while learning the paths. Canemo - Trained To Trial.pdf

This is not a new Turns progression. Java already knows how to turn.

We’re asking:

Can you use those mechanics around an obstacle/person while maintaining heel?
steps.todayJob: One direction at a time. Preserve the heel; don’t chase the figure eight.
steps.criterion: Java can navigate both left- and right-hand group paths while maintaining her established heel picture and appropriate body mechanics.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Neither direction requires special handling from Kerrie and the next meaningful question is whether Java can connect them.

steps.name: 3️⃣ CONNECT THE GROUP PATTERN
steps.goal: Java moves continuously through both sides of the group pattern while maintaining heel.
steps.actions:
Enter the group.

Complete one established path.

Continue directly into the opposite path.

Initially reinforce strategically inside the pattern rather than making exiting the group the only place anything good happens.

Use short combinations:
entry → one side → reward

then

entry → opposite side → reward

then

entry → both sides → reward.

Keep duration variable.

If one side deteriorates when connected, separate it again and repair that piece rather than rehearsing an increasingly ugly complete pattern.

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy.
steps.description:
Now connect the pieces.

Canemo’s clumping material specifically uses “one little loop in the group” as an example of taking a manageable piece of the BH routine instead of immediately running the entire exercise.

So don’t go from isolated turns straight to drilling the whole fucking trial picture.
steps.todayJob: Connect the paths without losing the heeling picture.
steps.criterion: Java can connect the left- and right-hand group paths fluidly while maintaining engagement, position, and appropriate body mechanics.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The connected pattern itself is understood and you’re ready to ask whether the same behavior survives actual people as the group.

steps.name: 4️⃣ REAL PEOPLE
steps.goal: Java performs the established group behavior around actual people.
steps.actions:
Replace chairs progressively with neutral people.

Don’t simultaneously make every variable harder.

Start with familiar, boring people standing neutrally.

Then vary:

* individuals,
* spacing,
* appearance,
* small normal movements,
* unfamiliar people.

Continue rewarding before likely attention loss.

If Java struggles with a particular person, don’t turn Group into a distraction-correction exercise. Increase space or simplify the path enough that she can perform the established behavior.

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy.
steps.description:
Now the geometry is no longer the hard part.

People are.

Canemo treats people as a predictable attention challenge and recommends a high reinforcement rate around them—approaching, entering, and moving around the group—rather than waiting until the dog has already disengaged.
steps.todayJob: Same fucking exercise. Now the cones have faces.
steps.criterion: Java maintains her established group-heeling behavior around multiple real people without significant attraction, avoidance, environmental scanning, or deterioration of heel.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Real people no longer fundamentally change the behavior and Java is ready for the complete group picture.

steps.name: 5️⃣ COMPLETE GROUP PICTURE
steps.goal: Java performs the complete group portion as an established piece ready to be consumed by BH clumping.
steps.actions:
Run the complete established group sequence with Kerrie behaving normally.

Vary reinforcement so Java doesn’t learn that one particular person, turn, halt, or group exit always predicts payment.

Begin reducing reinforcement within the group while still occasionally paying there to preserve value.

Use different groups of people and different locations as Java becomes successful.

Don’t start endlessly repeating the whole BH heeling routine just because the Group component works.

That’s what Clumping is for.

🎁 Reinforcer

Toy, progressively moved outside the immediate group sequence as Java becomes fluent.
steps.description:
Now assemble the actual exercise picture from the pieces Java already owns:

approach → enter → navigate group → required halt/basic position → continue/exit as appropriate.

Automatic Halt is consumed here, not retaught here.
steps.todayJob: Make the group a finished exercise, not a survival test.
steps.criterion: Java enters, navigates both directions around real people, performs the required halt/basic position, and completes the group picture while preserving her established heeling behavior without additional handler help.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

The group is reliable enough that Group itself no longer needs developmental training. Individual problems can be repaired within their owning components, while the finished Group behavior moves into BH clumping/trial preparation.

components.name: 1️⃣ BUILD THE GROUP ENTRY
components.finishedPicture:
Java enters the group in established heel and maintains engaged, correct heeling while moving closely around people in both directions, including the left- and right-hand portions of the group pattern. She adjusts her body appropriately to Kerrie’s path without forging, swinging wide, crabbing, lagging, or losing attention to the people.

Java can complete the required group pattern and halt in the group while maintaining the same heeling picture she has outside the group. People do not become the exercise; they are simply part of the environment in which Java heels.

exercises.name: GROUP / FIGURE-EIGHT HEELING
exercises.criteria:
Java enters the group in established heel and maintains engaged, correct heeling while moving closely around people in both directions, including the left- and right-hand portions of the group pattern. She adjusts her body appropriately to Kerrie’s path without forging, swinging wide, crabbing, lagging, or losing attention to the people.

Java can complete the required group pattern and halt in the group while maintaining the same heeling picture she has outside the group. People do not become the exercise; they are simply part of the environment in which Java heels.
exercises.notes:
Do not reteach these inside Group.

Java’s existing Heeling work owns the heeling behavior. Her existing Turns work owns the mechanics of following Kerrie’s left and right turns. Her Automatic Halt component owns Kerrie stopping → Java independently sitting in basic position.

Group consumes those established skills and asks a new question:

Can Java preserve them while navigating closely around people?

Canemo specifically recommends initially using four chairs arranged as corners to teach the group paths and working the left and right sides separately before expecting the complete group picture. They also put a lot of reinforcement into the group because people are a predictable place for attention to deteriorate. Canemo - Trained To Trial.pdf

steps.name: PEOPLE, PASSERS-BY & SOCIAL INTERACTION
steps.goal: Java remains neutral while pedestrians move around her and Kerrie interacts with another person.
steps.actions:
Work individual pieces first:

person passes → person approaches → person crosses closely in front → several pedestrians → Kerrie stops and talks → handshake → Java settles beside Kerrie.

Don’t demand formal heeling.

Java’s job is:
move with Kerrie, remain neutral, respond when asked, recover immediately from normal environmental events.

Gradually vary people, clothing, movement, proximity and locations.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or social release/reward as appropriate.

This isn’t where I’d deliberately manufacture huge toy arousal. You’re reinforcing environmental competence and neutrality.
steps.description:
This establishes the basic traffic-test social picture before stacking moving vehicles, dogs, etc.

In the actual test, Java walks on a loose leash on Kerrie’s left, remains indifferent to pedestrians/traffic, is cut off by a passer-by, then moves through a group of at least six people. Someone addresses Kerrie and shakes her hand while Java sits or downs beside her.
steps.todayJob: People happen. Java doesn’t give a shit.
steps.criterion:
✅ Success Criterion

Java moves willingly on a loose leash through pedestrians, tolerates someone crossing closely, and remains calm beside Kerrie during a brief conversation/handshake.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Normal pedestrian interaction is no longer a meaningful behavioral event for Java.

components.name: PEOPLE, PASSERS-BY & SOCIAL INTERACTION
components.finishedPicture:
Encounter with a group of people
At the instructions of the judge, the dog handler, with his dog, walks toward a group of people (as if
out for a walk-in public). The judge follows / watches the team at a reasonable distance. Without formal commands the dog is to follow on the dog handler’s left side on a loosely hanging leash –
with the shoulder at the knee height of the dog handler (loose lead informal heel). The dog must
be neutral / unbothered / indifferent to the people, traffic and to the environment. During the walk
the dog handler will pass people and will be stopped by a stranger. The dog has to show itself in a
neutral manner (without stress / aggression etc.). The handler and the dog continue through a relaxed
larger group of people (recommended more than 6 persons), in the larger group of people a person
interacts with the dog handler and greets them with a hand shake and short discussion. The dog has to
sit, down or stand beside the dog handler and has to remain neutral, quiet during the short
conversation.

steps.name: CYCLISTS & FAST PASSING PEOPLE
steps.goal: Java remains neutral when people move quickly past her from behind and toward her from the front.
steps.actions:
Separate variables initially:

bike visible → bike moving → bike passes at distance → closer pass → overtakes from behind → approaches head-on → bell + pass.

Do the same progression with:
one jogger → multiple joggers → overtake → head-on pass.

Add skaters if available.

Don’t stack speed + proximity + surprise + noise before Java understands the picture.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or appropriate calm reward.
steps.description:
The official cyclist scenario contains something useful to train deliberately: a cyclist overtakes from behind, rings a bell, later approaches from the opposite direction and rings again. Java is positioned between Kerrie and the passing bicycle. 

The test separately includes at least two joggers overtaking without slowing and later returning toward the team; inline skaters can substitute.
steps.todayJob: Fast-moving humans are scenery, not prey and not a problem.
steps.criterion: Java remains neutral and controllable through approaching and overtaking bicycles/joggers/skaters, including the bicycle bell and close passage.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Direction, speed and reasonable proximity no longer meaningfully change Java’s response.

components.name: CYCLISTS & FAST PASSING PEOPLE
components.finishedPicture:
The dog is walking along a road /path with his dog handler and is passed by a bicyclist from behind
who rings a bell. After passing the dog by a good distance, the cyclist turns to again pass the
dog handler and dog. There will be another bell ring. The bike passing has to be done in such a way that the dog is between the dog handler and the bicyclist passing by. The dog has to see the bicyclists.

steps.name: CARS & TRAFFIC NOISE
steps.goal: Java remains calm and controllable around vehicles and sudden normal vehicle sounds.
steps.actions:
Build separately:

parked cars → walking between/along cars → engine starts → door closes/slams → moving traffic → car pulls alongside/stops → window lowers → stranger talks to Kerrie.

Then combine them.

Change vehicle types and locations rather than teaching Java that the silver Honda at the club is the fucking BH car. 😂

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or calm release/reward.
steps.description:
The BH picture isn’t merely walking beside parked cars.

The current test can include walking past several cars, one starting, another door slamming, and a vehicle stopping beside the team while its occupant lowers the window and speaks to Kerrie. Java must sit or down on command and remain calm around the cars and traffic noise.
steps.todayJob: Engines, doors and people in cars mean nothing.
steps.criterion: Java remains environmentally stable and responsive around parked and moving vehicles, engine starts, door slams and a vehicle stopping beside Kerrie for an interaction.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Normal vehicle movement and noise cease to produce meaningful behavioral deterioration.

components.name: CARS & TRAFFIC NOISE
components.finishedPicture:
The dog handler walks past several cars or a car running or a car driving past the dog. The dog and
handler interact with the car and driver when a car stops by them. The horn should be honked. The
driver may roll down the window and interact with the dog and handler. The dog has to stand, sit or
lie down by the handler during this interaction. The dog has to be quiet and neutral to the cars and all traffic noises. The judge may modify this as needed.

steps.name: OTHER DOGS IN TRAFFIC
steps.goal: Java remains neutral while another handler and dog approach and pass.
steps.actions:
Use appropriate neutral dogs.

Build:
large distance → parallel movement → opposing movement → passing → overtaking → closer trial-relevant encounters.

Practice both:
continue walking past
and
park Java in Sit/Down while dog passes.

Change dogs.

Don’t let successful repetitions turn into greetings afterward. The behavioral category you’re building is other dog exists and has nothing to do with Java.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or appropriate reward after successful neutrality.
steps.description:
The test specifically requires neutrality when overtaking and approaching another dog-handler team. Kerrie may repeat Heel or put Java into Sit or Down during the encounter. 

This isn’t dog interaction.

It’s dog irrelevance.
steps.todayJob: See dog. Continue having a fucking job.
steps.criterion: Java can approach, pass, and be overtaken by a neutral dog-handler team without reactive behavior or losing functional control.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Multiple unfamiliar neutral dogs can perform these movements without Java’s behavior materially changing.

components.name: OTHER DOGS IN TRAFFIC
components.finishedPicture:
In the case of passing or encountering another dog and his handler, the dog is to remain neutral.
The handler may give and repeat the command “Fuss/Heel” or place the dog in a stand, sit or down position.

steps.name: 1️⃣TETHERED + KERRIE OUT OF SIGHT
steps.goal: Java remains calm when temporarily tethered without Kerrie present.
steps.actions:
Do not begin with the complete picture.

Build:

tether → Kerrie one step away → greater distance → Kerrie briefly disappears → gradually increase out-of-sight duration.

Separately add:
pedestrian passes → normal environmental activity → neutral dog passes at generous distance.

Then progressively decrease the dog-pass distance toward the trial picture.

Only combine out of sight + traffic + passing dog once the individual questions are boring.

Java does not need a formal Down unless that’s the behavior you choose. The rules allow standing, sitting, or lying down. 

🎁 Reinforcer

Food/social reward when Kerrie returns, without making Kerrie’s reappearance an explosive event.
steps.description:
This deserves its own rung because it’s a completely different question from walking around traffic.

In the test, Java is tethered beside a moderately busy street and Kerrie goes out of sight into a shop/entrance. Java may stand, sit, or lie down. While Kerrie is gone, another person walks a leashed neutral dog past at approximately five paces lateral distance. Java must remain calm.
steps.todayJob: Kerrie disappears. Java’s world does not fucking end.
steps.criterion: Java remains calm while tethered with Kerrie completely out of sight and can tolerate ordinary environmental activity without vocal, reactive, or escape behavior.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Multiple unfamiliar neutral dogs can perform these movements without Java’s behavior materially changing.

steps.name: 2️⃣ TETHERED + KERRIE OUT OF SIGHT
steps.goal: Java remains calm when temporarily tethered without Kerrie present.
steps.actions:
Do not begin with the complete picture.

Build:

tether → Kerrie one step away → greater distance → Kerrie briefly disappears → gradually increase out-of-sight duration.

Separately add:
pedestrian passes → normal environmental activity → neutral dog passes at generous distance.

Then progressively decrease the dog-pass distance toward the trial picture.

Only combine out of sight + traffic + passing dog once the individual questions are boring.

Java does not need a formal Down unless that’s the behavior you choose. The rules allow standing, sitting, or lying down. 

🎁 Reinforcer

Food/social reward when Kerrie returns, without making Kerrie’s reappearance an explosive event.

In the test, Java is tethered beside a moderately busy street and Kerrie goes out of sight into a shop/entrance. Java may stand, sit, or lie down. While Kerrie is gone, another person walks a leashed neutral dog past at approximately five paces lateral distance. Java must remain calm.
steps.todayJob: Kerrie disappears. Java’s world does not fucking end.
steps.criterion: Java remains calm while tethered with Kerrie completely out of sight and can tolerate ordinary environmental activity without vocal, reactive, or escape behavior.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Out-of-sight tethering itself is stable and you’re ready to put the passing-dog picture into it.

steps.name: 3️⃣ TETHERED + PASSING DOG
steps.goal: Java performs the hardest combined tether picture required by the traffic test.
steps.actions:
Start easier than the final picture.

Tether Java.

Kerrie disappears.

Neutral dog passes at a comfortable distance.

Progressively approximate the official scenario until the dog can pass at roughly the required five-pace lateral distance while Kerrie remains out of sight. 

Vary:

* passing dog,
* direction,
* location,
* tether point,
* environmental activity.

Do not use reactive dogs to proof this. The FCI rule itself explicitly says the passing dog should not be reactive. 

🎁 Reinforcer

Food/social reward after Kerrie returns and the exercise is complete.
steps.description:
Now combine the established absence behavior with the established dog-neutrality behavior.

Kerrie disappears.

Another dog passes.

Nothing happens.
steps.todayJob: Alone + dog passes = still boring.
steps.criterion: With Kerrie out of sight, Java remains calm while an unfamiliar neutral leashed dog passes at approximately the trial distance.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can do this with different neutral dogs and locations without the picture becoming a significant event.

components.name: TETHERED + KERRIE OUT OF SIGHT
components.finishedPicture:
At the instruction of the judge, the dog handler stops and attaches the leash to a fence, wall, or
something similar. The dog handler goes out of sight. The dog may be left standing, sitting or
lying. During the absence of the dog handler, a passer-by (pedestrian) passes the dog with a dog at a lateral distance of about five paces away from the test dog. The dog left alone has to be quiet and calm (neutral) during the absence of the handler. The dog used to walk by must be a neutral dog (no dog

A dog showing aggression (strong pulling on the leash, continuous barking, hackles, barring teeth) will

impact the length of the trial)

steps.name: JOGGERS / INLINE SKATERS
steps.goal: Java remains neutral and under control when joggers or inline skaters overtake from behind and approach/pass from the opposite direction.
steps.actions:
Begin with enough distance that Java can easily remain neutral.

Progress through:

one jogger/skater visible → moving past at distance → closer passing → overtaking from behind → approaching from the front → multiple people moving together.

Then build the more complete test picture:

Kerrie and Java walking → at least two joggers/skaters overtake without slowing → continue walking → joggers/skaters later approach from the opposite direction and pass.

Vary:

* Joggers versus inline skaters
* Individual people
* Clothing
* Speed
* Passing distance
* Direction
* One versus multiple people
* Location

Don’t deliberately stack novel person + high speed + close proximity + novel location if Java hasn’t demonstrated the individual pieces yet.

And don’t turn it into formal Fuss. Java’s job is simply:

Move with Kerrie. Fast humans happen. Keep functioning.

🎁 Reinforcer

Food or calm social reward, particularly while building neutrality to the picture.
steps.description:
This is its own traffic-test picture, separate from cyclists.

Java needs to understand that fast-moving people coming from behind, passing close by, or approaching head-on are environmental background. She does not need formal competition heeling here; she needs to remain neutral, controllable, and socially appropriate.

Build joggers first or skaters first based on availability. Once one is boring, generalize the same concept to the other rather than assuming Java automatically considers them equivalent.
steps.todayJob: People can haul ass past Java without becoming Java’s business.
steps.criterion: Java remains calm, neutral, and controllable while joggers or inline skaters overtake from behind and while they approach/pass from the opposite direction, including when multiple people move past together.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can perform the complete passing/overtaking picture with both joggers and inline skaters when available, across different people and locations, without their speed, direction, or proximity materially changing her behavior.

components.name: JOGGERS / INLINE SKATERS
components.finishedPicture:
The dog handler walks along a road / path with his dog. At least one jogger / skater or more pass
him without slowing down and after passing the handler and dog the jogger / skater (s) will turn
and pass again on the opposite side. The dog does not have be in correct (formal) heel position,
but he must not bother (remain neutral) the passing joggers. It is permitted to have the handler place his dog in a stand, sit or down position during the encounter

steps.name: COMPLETE TRAFFIC TEST PICTURE
steps.goal: Java generalizes the individual skills into the unpredictable public-environment evaluation required for BH/VT.
steps.actions:
Run traffic-test outings containing some, not necessarily all, established elements:

pedestrians, groups, greeting/handshake, cyclist, bell, joggers/skaters, cars/noise, other dogs, tethering and absence.

Change locations.

Change order.

Change people.

Change dogs.

Change vehicles.

Occasionally run a complete mock test, but don’t make every training day a full rehearsal.

🎁 Reinforcer

Initially reinforce between scenarios as necessary; progressively move reinforcement outside larger chunks as Java demonstrates stability.
steps.description:
This is important because the judge isn’t required to reproduce one memorized script. The regulations explicitly allow the exercises to be adapted to local conditions and repeated or varied if the judge is uncertain. 

So Java shouldn’t learn the traffic routine.

She needs the concept:

Normal weird shit happens in public → remain neutral, controllable and environmentally stable.
steps.todayJob: Java doesn’t memorize the test. Java understands the world.
steps.criterion: Across unfamiliar public locations and changing combinations of the required traffic-test categories, Java remains calm, neutral, confident, controllable and responsive to Kerrie without needing training management that won’t exist in the test.
steps.rule:
➡️ Advance When

Java can walk into a novel but reasonable public BH-type environment and the specific arrangement of people, vehicles, dogs and movement doesn’t materially matter anymore.
